newsitem.title: INDIA: India SBI deposits up 15 pct in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: India SBI deposits up 15 pct in 96/97.

text.p: India's largest commercial bank, the state-run State Bank of India (SBI), said on Thursday its domestic deposits had grown 15.1 percent during the financial year 1996/97 (April-March).
"The domestic deposits of the Bank stood at 1,037.67 billion rupees as at end-March 1997, thus crossing the landmark in deposit level of 1,000 billion rupees," SBI said in a statement.
"The domestic deposits of the Bank recorded a growth of 15.1 percent during the year, which was higher than 12.3 percent growth recorded last year."

SBI said deposits in its personal banking segment, a stable and low-cost source of funds, had grown 22 percent to constitute a 56 percent share of its deposits. SBI's NRI deposits grew 30 percent, to 128.48 billion rupees by year's end.

The bank said its credit deployment process had been affected by the depressed market for credit, with net domestic credit rising only 6.2 percent, to 550.23 billion, at the end of March, compared to 25.7 percent growth the previous year.
